div.div: Resource claims decide what may overlap: one physical action, one gaze lease and one conversation turn can run together, but two physical actions never can, because each needs the one action slot

PHYSICAL ACTION
wave, expression, handshake, canned robot TTS, composites

GAZE LEASE
set / clear a gaze target; priority derived from the gaze mode

SESSION SERVICE
conversation turn, enrolment, gift offer, greeting, operator alert

nothing, or
exclusive via an
output lease

NOT CLAIMABLE
listening is the kernel's visitor-audio permit, not a resource

WHAT FOLLOWS (B3)
- Every physical action claims the one action slot, so two physical actions never run at once.
- Concurrency exists only BETWEEN kinds: one physical action + one gaze lease + one conversation turn.
- Head and gaze drive the same actuators: no primitive claims both; an exclusive-head primitive is refused while a gaze lease is active.
- Conversation speech (session service on an output lease) may overlap a wave; canned robot TTS cannot, it occupies the slot. A line + gesture is ONE composite primitive.

CONFLICT MATRIX (closed; no primitive or experience may override it, B4): action slot - an equal-or-lower priority request is deferred, a higher one preempts and waits for the old command's terminal cancellation | gaze - refuses lower priority, replaces at equal or higher after the prior clear succeeds | audio out - a conflict is refused | safety priority is reserved for the kernel
THE SHOWCASE SCENARIO (C2), with the conservative first wave primitive (slot + body + head, all exclusive, no audio). Order only: the notes give no durations, so bar lengths are a drawing choice.

Between 3 and 4 the gaze lease is cleared WITH acknowledgement before the wave starts: the wave claims the head exclusively. A lighter arm-only wave would be a later catalog revision with its own scenario (B3).

The video only illustrates the overlaps. The proof is the held intervals in the evidence (acquired -> released per invocation), read from evidence fields, never inferred from presentation events (C2).

Legend: matrix - solid amber = claim always held (exclusive) | dashed light amber = optional claim | white '-' = never claimed | red = not a resource. Timeline - amber = gaze lease, green = physical action, purple = conversation turn; dashed verticals = the seven showcase steps in order.

Sources. Mechanisms: this kit's notes/ (named per line below) and glossary.md. Every number is loaded from ../constants.json by the key shown: [Pn] = public (cited); [In] = illustrative (a round design parameter that keeps the design's relations; never a measurement of any system); [calc] = my arithmetic on tagged values.
Mechanism: notes/B3-the-effect-vocabulary.md (contract kinds, resources and permitted claims, action slot, head vs gaze, speech vs canned TTS, composite primitives, conservative first wave claims); B4-kernel-interception-and-arbitration.md (closed conflict matrix); C2-the-conformance-ladder.md (showcase scenario order, held intervals, 'the video illustrates, the evidence proves'). This page carries no numeric design parameter.
